title: Sections over a quasi-compact quasi-separated etale object commute with filtered colimits of sheaves of modules
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $X_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $\Lambda$ a commutative ring and $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the category of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $U\to X$ be an object of $X_{\Et}$ such that the scheme $U$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\mathcal I$ be a small filtered category, $i\mapsto\mathcal G_i$ a diagram $\mathcal I\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and $(\mathcal G,(c_i)_{i})$ a colimit of it in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then the canonical map
$$
\Psi:\varinjlim_{i\in\mathcal I}\mathcal G_i(U)\longrightarrow\mathcal G(U),
$$
the unique map (colimit of the sets, equivalently of the $\Lambda$-modules $\mathcal G_i(U)$) whose composite with the coprojection of $\mathcal G_i(U)$ is $(c_i)_U$, is bijective. This is Sites, Lemma Tag 0738, part (4), with the etale-site cofinality supplied by Etale Cohomology, Section 59.51, Tag 03Q4.

source.place: Sites, Lemma 7.17.7, Tag 0738 (label lemma-directed-colimits-sections), part (4), applied to the etale site using Etale Cohomology, Section 59.51, Tag 03Q4 (label section-colimit), first paragraph

proof.text: *Finite refinements.* The public node [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-cofinal-finite-coverings], proved from Etale Cohomology Tag 03Q4 and the affine-etale refinement, supplies the following fact used in the next two steps: every covering of the quasi-compact quasi-separated object $U$ has a refinement $\{V_b\to U\}_{b\in B}$ with $B$ finite, each $V_b$ affine and etale over $U$, and each fibre product $V_b\times_UV_{b'}$ quasi-compact. The refinement is cofinal, so it may be applied both to a covering witnessing an equality after sheafification and to a covering representing a sheafified section.

source.place: Section 59.51, Tag 03Q4, first paragraph, together with Sites, Lemma Tag 0738

proof.text: *Injectivity.* Put $\mathcal P(V)=\varinjlim_{i\in\mathcal I}\mathcal G_i(V)$ for the sectionwise presheaf colimit. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], the underlying sheaf of $\mathcal G$ is the sheafification $\mathcal P^\#$ of $\mathcal P$. Suppose $s\in\mathcal G_i(U)$ and $s'\in\mathcal G_{i'}(U)$ have equal images in $\mathcal G(U)$. The local sheafification statement [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] (Sites, Tags 00WB and 00WK) gives a covering on which the restrictions of the two sections of $\mathcal P$ agree. Apply the cofinal refinement from Step 1 to obtain a finite family $\{V_b\to U\}_{b\in B}$. For each $b$, equality in the filtered colimit $\mathcal P(V_b)$ is eventual by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], so there is an index $k_b$ above $i$ and $i'$ at which the two restrictions agree. Filteredness gives one index $k$ above the finite family $(k_b)_{b\in B}$. The sheaf equalizer condition [lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition] then gives equality of the transported sections in $\mathcal G_k(U)$, proving that $\Psi$ is injective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0738, proof of part (2), using Theorem Tag 00WB and Lemma Tag 00WK for the local sheafification description

proof.text: *Surjectivity.* Let $t\in\mathcal G(U)$. The local sheafification statement [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] supplies a covering $\{W_a\to U\}_{a\in A}$ and sections $p_a\in\mathcal P(W_a)$ whose sheafified images are the restrictions of $t$, with pairwise compatibility after further coverings. Apply the cofinal refinement from Step 1 to obtain a finite family $\{V_b\to U\}_{b\in B}$, each factoring through some $W_{a(b)}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], choose $i_b\in\mathcal I$ and $t_b\in\mathcal G_{i_b}(V_b)$ representing the restriction of $p_{a(b)}$. On $V_b\times_UV_{b'}$ the images of $t_b$ and $t_{b'}$ in $\mathcal G$ agree because both restrict from $t$. This overlap is quasi-compact by Step 1, so injectivity from Step 2 gives an index $i_{bb'}$ where the two restrictions agree. Choose one index $i$ dominating the finitely many $i_b$ and $i_{bb'}$. The transported sections in $\mathcal G_i(V_b)$ agree on every pairwise fibre product, hence glue by [lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition] to a section $t_i\in\mathcal G_i(U)$ mapping to $t$. The underlying-set and module statements agree by the forgetful-colimit tool [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Thus $\Psi$ is surjective and bijective.
